issues: [High/Repetition & monotony] The exact phrase 'Jeg kan godt lide at spille badminton' (or 'Jeg elsker at spille badminton') is declared in almost every scene. — While grammatical repetition is useful for A1, having Maya state or think this exact sentence in scenes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 crosses into a robotic refrain. It should be varied, implied, or omitted in some of the scenes to preserve a natural narrative flow.

[High/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Unnatural over-repetition of 'I like/love to play badminton' — Maya states 'Jeg elsker/kan godt lide at spille badminton' in 6 out of the 7 scenes. While some repetition reinforces grammar, having her repeatedly declare this exact phrase out loud—to the kiosk worker in Scene 3, then twice to Kasper and Sara in Scenes 5 and 6—makes her sound like a robot and breaks the immersion of the dialogue.

[Med/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Emil disappears without a trace after Scene 4 — Emil is explicitly introduced in Scene 4 to make a four-player doubles match and hits the shuttlecock. However, in Scene 5's post-match chat and Scene 6's cafeteria visit, only Kasper and Sara are mentioned. Emil vanishes completely without a goodbye, leaving the learner wondering where the fourth player went.

[High/Repetition & monotony] Extreme overuse of the exact phrase 'Jeg kan godt lide / elsker at spille badminton'. — This specific sentence appears in almost every single scene (scenes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6). While reinforcing the grammar focus is intended, having the protagonist repeat this exact same line repeatedly—often abruptly in dialogue or thought—is highly unnatural and noticeable.

[Med/Repetition & monotony] Repetitive scene transitions (ending a scene with an action and starting the next with the exact same action). — The transitions between scenes 2/3, 3/4, and 5/6 follow an identical formula. Scene 2 ends 'går hen til kiosken' and Scene 3 starts 'går hen til en lille kiosk'; Scene 3 ends 'går over til banerne' and Scene 4 starts 'går over til en badmintonbane'; Scene 5 ends by deciding to go to the cafeteria, and Scene 6 starts 'Vi går ind i det lille cafeteria'. This makes the storytelling feel tedious.

[High/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Robotic repetition of the phrase 'I like/love to play badminton' — Maya explicitly states 'Jeg elsker at spille badminton' or 'Jeg kan godt lide at spille badminton' in scenes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. Dropping this exact phrase into almost every scene—like blurting it out to the kiosk clerk in Scene 3 or unprompted at the cafeteria table in Scene 6—makes her sound like a programmed robot rather than a person.

[Low/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Emil disappears without a trace after the match — Emil is specifically introduced by name in Scene 4 so they have four players for doubles. However, once the match ends in Scene 5, only Kasper, Sara, and Maya are mentioned as walking off, drinking water, and going to the cafeteria. Emil vanishes entirely. A tiny nod to him leaving would tie off this loose end.

[High/Repetition & monotony] The exact phrase "Jeg kan godt lide at spille badminton" (or "Jeg elsker at...") is a constant refrain. — Maya states that she likes or loves to play badminton in Scene 1, Scene 2, Scene 3, Scene 4, Scene 5, and Scene 6. While reinforcing the grammar target (*godt kan lide at*) is intended, repeating the exact same sentence about badminton in almost every single scene sounds highly robotic and unnatural.

[High/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Overuse of the exact phrase 'Jeg kan godt lide / elsker at spille badminton' as dialogue. — While reinforcing the target grammar is good, Maya declares this exact phrase in almost every scene. Saying it unprompted to the kiosk worker (Scene 3), after the match (Scene 5), and again out of nowhere at the cafe table (Scene 6) makes her sound like a pull-string toy rather than a person holding a conversation.
